name: Nara
days: 1 (day trip, solo, while friend is in Hokkaido)
overview: Famous for over 1,000 free-roaming sacred deer that bow for crackers (shika-senbei) in exchange. Winter is a genuinely good time to visit, not a downside.

recommendations.title: Nara Park deer
recommendations.summary: Present year-round; winter brings fewer crowds and snow-dusted deer.
recommendations.body: Present year-round, unaffected by winter since deer don't hibernate. Winter brings fewer tourists and a chance of snow-dusted deer for striking photos. Deer near the entrance are more assertive/handsy than ones further into the park — keep bags zipped, watch loose straps.

recommendations.title: Shikayose (deer calling)
recommendations.body: 10am on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays in Jan/Feb 2026, at Tobihino near Kasuga Taisha. Staff blow a horn and deer gather from the woods — a winter-only tradition (less natural food available, so they're drawn in more reliably). Worth building the morning around if the day trip lands on a weekend.

recommendations.title: Todai-ji
recommendations.summary: Giant Buddha hall, one of the world's largest wooden buildings.
recommendations.body: One of several stops rather than the main draw, but easy to combine since it's inside/adjacent to the park.

recommendations.title: Kasuga Taisha
recommendations.summary: The shrine tied to the deer legend.
recommendations.body: The shrine tied to the deer legend — a deity is said to have ridden a deer to Nara. Pairs naturally with the deer-calling event.

recommendations.title: Nara Park itself
recommendations.summary: The whole park is a large, forested green space, not just deer-viewing.
recommendations.body: The walk between Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha passes through genuine woodland — the whole park is a large, forested green space, not just a deer-viewing area.

recommendations.title: Kasugayama Primeval Forest
recommendations.summary: Old-growth forest, UNESCO World Heritage site.
recommendations.body: Old-growth forest bordering Kasuga Taisha, a UNESCO World Heritage site — a real step up in "nature" from the main park if more forest time is wanted.

recommendations.title: Mount Wakakusa
recommendations.summary: Hill with walking trails and open views over Nara.
recommendations.body: A hill just behind the park with walking trails and open views over Nara from the top — more effort than the flat park paths but not a full hike.
